intent: One chosen value of a multiple-value Combobox, shown as a pill with a button that removes it.
typical_uses: One chosen value inside ComboboxChips, rendered for one entry of the value

dont_use_when.situation: A status or category tag that is not a chosen value

invariants.text: A chip stands for the chosen value at its own position among the chips: the remove button, and Backspace or Delete while the chip has focus, remove the value at that index of the root's value, whatever the chip's caption says.
The remove button takes no keyboard focus (the primitive gives it `tabIndex` -1); keyboard users reach the chip itself with the arrow keys from the input and remove it with Backspace or Delete.

anti_patterns.dont: Render chips in an order, or a number, different from the root's value
anti_patterns.do_instead: Render exactly one chip per chosen value, in the value's order, typically from ComboboxValue's function child; a chip removes the value at its own index

a11y.by: the primitive's Combobox.ChipRemove renders a native button; combobox.test.tsx asserts the remove button is found by role button and the default name "Remove", or "Entfernen" when `removeLabel` is passed, and that pressing it reports the value without that chip through onValueChange

children.states: children is the chip's caption, any React content
children.because: `ReactNode` is a union of elements, strings, numbers, fragments and more, which the compiler cannot state as one JSON type.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the chip's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the chip's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (disabled). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through combobox.module.css, not through this.

unexposed_parts.reason: Composed inside ComboboxChip behind `showRemove`; only its accessible name is exposed, as `removeLabel`.

good.title: A chip whose remove button names its value
A fixed chip with no remove button

bad.title: A chip outside ComboboxChips
bad.why: The primitive's Chip reads the enclosing ComboboxChips through context and throws when there is none; place the chips inside ComboboxChips.

children.description: Partially typed: ReactNode. The compiler emits one JSON type per property and none for this one; shape checked by tsc, see x-uikit.partially_typed_props. children is the chip's caption, any React content. `ReactNode` is a union of elements, strings, numbers, fragments and more, which the compiler cannot state as one JSON type.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, ComboboxChipState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the chip's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.description: TS: CSSProperties | ((state: ComboboxChipState) => CSSProperties | undefined) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. style accepts a function of the chip's state as well as a plain style object. Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (disabled). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through combobox.module.css, not through this.
